discovery: Discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the opening of neutrino astronomy with the IceCube Neutrino Observatory
motivation: Francis Halzen conceived, championed and led IceCube, which turned a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a neutrino telescope. In 2013 IceCube established a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies, well above the atmospheric background and at high statistical significance. Since then, independent analyses have confirmed it, and it has been followed by evidence for neutrino emission from the blazar TXS 0506+056 (2017), the Seyfert galaxy NGC 1068 (2022) and the Galactic plane (2023). Together these results opened a new observational window on the non-thermal universe: neutrinos trace hadronic cosmic-ray accelerators that photons cannot reveal unambiguously. The results rest on careful likelihood analyses, blind procedures and pre-defined thresholds, and the measurements have been reproduced with growing datasets. This is a genuine discovery that created a field, namely multimessenger neutrino astronomy, and it rests on an audacious instrument that Halzen made real.
